title: Rabbi Elazar bar Avina
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Yevamot 63a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.63a.11), saying: “Calamity comes to the world only on account of Israel.” In [Berakhot 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.4b.16), Rabbi Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Avina: “Whoever says ‘Praise of David’…,” etc. Hyman proposes Rabbi Elazar bar Avina for this attribution and reports that Ein Yaakov and Dikdukei Soferim read that way. He is likewise mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:5, folio 10. In Bereshit Rabbah 98:2 Rabbi Yehudah speaks in his name — he is Rabbi Yudan, as the statement is cited in Midrash Tehillim 31:7. At the beginning of Pesikta deRav Kahana we find Rabbi Tanchum his son-in-law, and Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on “I have come into my garden,” reads Rabbi Menachem his son-in-law.

notes.text: תהלה לדוד is rendered “Praise of David,” preserving the distinction from a מזמור. The bar-versus-said-that emendation, Yehudah/Yudan identification and Tanchum/Menachem sons-in-law remain Hyman’s supplied claims. Folio 10 has no side supplied.

The inspected Yevamot 63a names Elazar bar Avina and explicitly says that calamity comes only on account of Israel. The exact Ein Yaakov/Dikdukei Soferim readings and the Yehudah/Yudan and Tanchum/Menachem relations remain Hyman’s supplied claims.

The consulted [Berakhot 4b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.4b.16) gives Rabbi Elazar in Rabbi Avina’s name. At [4b:23](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.4b.23), Rabbi Elazar bar Avina is named for a different teaching, about Michael and Gabriel. The second passage attests the patronymic without settling the reading of the Psalm attribution.
